summary: This bill amends federal criminal law to require that anyone convicted of producing, distributing, receiving, or possessing child pornography or related obscene material be fined and sentenced to death or life in prison.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends criminal penalties in Title 18 for child pornography offenses but contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budgets. It has no bearing on government spending.
The bill focuses exclusively on criminal penalties and makes no changes to tax law, rates, or enforcement. No relation to taxation.
No provisions address healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services. Irrelevant to the topic.
The legislation concerns child pornography penalties and has no connection to firearms regulation or Second Amendment issues.
No immigration, border, or visa provisions appear in the bill text.
The bill does not address reproductive rights or abortion access in any way.
No military, defense, or national security spending measures are included.
The bill contains no environmental, energy, or regulatory provisions.
No welfare, entitlement, or social services programs are mentioned or altered.
The legislation does not touch on schools, education funding, or curriculum.
Child pornography penalties are unrelated to controlled substances or drug enforcement policy.

The bill directly amends multiple sections of Title 18 to replace existing penalties for child pornography possession, receipt, distribution, and related offenses with mandatory fines plus death or life imprisonment. This constitutes a substantial increase in sentencing severity for these crimes and aligns strongly with tougher sentencing policies.
No trade, tariff, or international commerce provisions are present.
The bill has no fiscal impact language or implications for deficits or debt.
No provisions address sexual orientation, gender identity, or related civil rights.
The legislation does not reference foreign assistance or international aid.
No election administration, voting rights, or campaign provisions exist.
While child pornography involves digital material, the bill addresses only criminal penalties and does not regulate technology companies, data privacy, or surveillance practices.
No labor, employment, or union-related content is included.
The bill contains no religious exemptions, anti-discrimination rules, or conscience protections.
